newsitem.title: USA: Talks continue between Ford, UAW bargainers.
newsitem.headline: Talks continue between Ford, UAW bargainers.

text.p: Contract talks continued Saturday between Ford Motor Co. and the United Auto Workers (UAW), but disagreements over outsourcing issues threatened to push negotiations on a new labor pact past the midnight deadline.
Bargainers were optimistic, according to Ford spokesman Jon Harmon, but they remained apart on key issues.
"They're not there yet on all the issues. It's going to take a while to get through," Harmon told reporters staked out at Ford's headquarters in Dearborn.
"The main point is we think we can do this without a work stoppage," he said, adding that by mid-afternoon there had been no talk of extending the deadline.
Talks broke off before midnight on Friday, and members of several key subcommittees arrived at Ford World Headquarters here with suitcases on Saturday morning.

Earlier Ford officials said they expected to get a new deal by the time the current contract expires at midnight. Bargainers are believed to have generally agreed on a three-year deal that would give Ford's 105,000 UAW members a 2 percent base wage increase each year.
But union efforts to protect jobs and restrict outsourcing -- the practice of farming out parts work to outside suppliers -- have been key issues during the current round of talks.

Ford is leading negotiations for the next contracts covering nearly 400,000 UAW hourly workers at Ford, General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp In the last negotiations in 1993, also led by Ford, it took a marathon 40-hour bargaining session and a nearly 24-hour contract extension to reach a settlement.
Meantime, officials at UAW locals around the country said they were prepared to go on strike if they get the call from their representatives in Dearborn.
The UAW on Friday extended its contracts with GM and Chrysler, pledging not to strike those automakers while it continues bargaining with Ford.
